candidates: When deleting or renaming a documentation page, update both `idRedirectMap` and `urlRedirectMap` in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/redirect.ts`. Also verify that no remaining entries in either map use the removed/old path as a redirect *destination*; stale targets cause broken redirects even when the source key is correctly updated.

Format badge/shield image links in Markdown documentation with one badge per line rather than concatenating all badges into a single long line. This keeps diffs readable and prevents very long lines that are hard to review.

Third-party tools and integrations not maintained by the mermaid-js GitHub organization should be placed in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/ecosystem/integrations.md`, not listed alongside official sibling projects in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/intro/index.md`. Listing them there implies organizational ownership and maintenance responsibility that the project does not have.

New documentation source files added under `packages/mermaid/src/docs` must use kebab-case file names (e.g. `questions-and-suggestions.md`), not camelCase or PascalCase, to maintain naming consistency with the existing file set. Renaming established files requires extra redirect entries and is deferred work, so it is important not to introduce new non-kebab names.

When documenting that documentation-only pull requests may target the `master` branch directly, explicitly state that the contributor's working branch must also be *based on* `master`, not `develop`. Omitting this causes contributors to open PRs with `develop` commits mixed in.

Proofread prose in documentation for grammatical accuracy, including correct preposition choice (e.g. 'Create a Pull Request from the branch in your fork', not 'of your fork') and correct article/clause structure. These small errors erode trust in the documentation.

When a documentation code block is meant to show Markdown-formatted content, use the `markdown` language specifier (` ```markdown `) rather than a plain unlabeled fence. This enables syntax highlighting in the rendered docs site and signals to readers that the content is Markdown.
